evals.prompt: Edit this customer email for clarity and concision. Keep its factual limits and respectful tone: 'Hi Morgan, I wanted to take a moment to provide an update on today's import issue. The import stopped at 9:10 a.m. We restarted the worker at 9:42 a.m., and new imports are now processing. We are still checking whether any records from the interrupted batch need to be retried, so I cannot yet say that all records are present. I will send you the result of that check by 11 a.m. Thank you for your patience.'
evals.expected_output: A short, courteous email retaining the 9:10 stop, 9:42 restart, resumed new imports, unresolved record check, and 11 a.m. update. It must not claim all records are present.

evals.prompt: Edit this pull request description for clarity and concision: 'We are excited to announce that this PR introduces a highly useful improvement to the upload process. Before, a network timeout meant an upload failed immediately. Now, the worker retries timeouts up to three times with backoff. This change is important because users on unstable connections can finish uploads. I ran pytest tests/test_upload.py: 18 passed. I did not run the full suite. One thing worth noting is that permanent failures still need a manual retry. In conclusion, this PR makes uploads more robust.'
evals.expected_output: A concise PR body retaining the old and new behavior, reason, retry limit and backoff, exact test result and scope, and manual retry limitation. No unsupported assurance or ceremonial introduction/conclusion.
